sassanid.title: Derafsh Kaviani
sassanid.subtitle: Legendary royal standard of Persia (Sassanid Empire)

colors.note: The standard was said to be made of leather adorned with jewels and precious metals.

desc:
- The Derafsh Kaviani (درفش کاویانی) was the legendary royal standard of the Sassanid Empire
- According to the Shahnameh, Kaveh the Blacksmith raised his leather apron on a spear to rally
- the people against the tyrant Zahhak. The banner was captured by Arab forces at the
- Battle of al-Qadisiyyah in 636 CE
- **Construction:** a leather or cloth banner (drafsh) featuring the Derafsh Kaviani — a legendary royal standard often depicted as a rectangular jewelled leather apron on a pole
trivia:
- The Sassanid Empire (224–651) was the last Persian Empire before Islamic conquest
- Represented one of history's great empires alongside Rome
- Known for advanced administrative and military systems

sassanid-alt.title: Derafsh Kaviani (alternate)
sassanid-alt.subtitle: Legendary royal standard of Persia (Sassanid Empire)
desc:
- An alternative representation of the Sassanid Empire's banner, typically featuring the Derafsh Kaviani — a legendary royal standard with streamers and precious stones
- The Sassanid Empire (224–651 CE) was the last pre-Islamic Persian empire
- Their royal banners were elaborate, jewelled standards rather than simple cloth flags
- **Construction:** varies; the Derafsh Kaviani was a leather apron mounted on a lance, adorned with jewels. No standard ratio
trivia:
- Alternative Sassanid flag design with different symbolism
- Represents variations in royal banners and regalia
- Shows the evolution of Sassanid heraldic traditions

qajar.title: Flag of the Qajar Dynasty
desc: - The Qajar Dynasty (1789–1925) used a tricolour-style flag featuring a lion holding a sword with the rising sun behind it — the Shir-o-Khorshid
- **Construction:** a white or green field bearing the Lion and Sun motif, with variations by specific Qajar rulers
trivia:
- The Qajar dynasty (1785–1925) ruled Persia and modernised Iran
- The lion and sun represented Persian power and mythology
- Preceded the Pahlavi dynasty

pahlavi.title: Flag of the Pahlavi Dynasty (Imperial Iran)
desc: - The Pahlavi Dynasty (1925–1979) used the green-white-red tricolour with the lion-and-sun emblem. This was replaced after the 1979 Islamic Revolution
- **Construction:** three equal horizontal bands of green, white, and red with the Lion and Sun emblem (a lion passant carrying a sword, backed by a rising sun) centred on the white band
trivia:
- The Pahlavi dynasty (1925–1979) ruled Iran under Reza Shah and Mohammad Reza Shah
- The lion and sun symbolised Persian power and mythology
- Overthrown in the Iranian Revolution of 1979
